title: Electronics Hardware Technology Parks Strengthen India’s Export Oriented Electronics Manufacturing Ecosystem
subtitle: EHTP Units Rise to 79, with Exports Crossing ₹11,100 Crore in FY 2025-26
body_text:
The EHTP Scheme is a 100% export-oriented scheme to promote exports of electronic hardware from India and STPI has been providing Statutory Services on a single-window Clearance System under EHTP Scheme. There is no fund allocation under the EHTP scheme.
Details regarding EHTP units for the last three years are tabled below:
FY 2023-24 FY 2024-25 FY 2025-26 Total No of EHTP Units 70 73 79 Total Exports by EHTP Units (In Rs. Crore) 9,678 11,443 11,102*
*Estimated

The incentives and fiscal benefits available to eligible EHTP units are governed by the provisions of the Foreign Trade Policy 2023. These include:
● Duty-free import/procurement of capital goods, raw materials, components, consumables, spares, and other permitted goods required for export production, subject to the provisions of the Foreign Trade Policy
● Permission for Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) sales in accordance with the provisions of the Foreign Trade Policy
● Other operational and procedural benefits, including simplified customs procedures and single-window statutory clearances
Following measures have been taken to promote investment and expand participation under the EHTP Scheme:
● Automation of Statutory Services: For providing seamless services to the EHTP units, STPI has automated statutory services through digital platform, its approval and final intimation to them. This has ensured speedy delivery of services to the satisfaction of the industry.
● Simplification of Import Procedures: The earlier practice of case-to-case import permissions has been replaced with blanket import permissions for the financial year concerned.
● Promotion and Industry Outreach: Regular stakeholder consultations, awareness programmes, industry interactions, and participation in trade events are organised to create awareness about the EHTP Scheme and encourage new investments.
This information was given by Union Minister of State for Electronics and IT Shri Jitin Prasada in Lok Sabha on 12.08.2026

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, the Minister of State for Electronics and IT stated that the number of Electronics Hardware Technology Park (EHTP) units rose from 70 in FY 2023-24 to 79 in FY 2025-26, with exports estimated at ₹11,102 crore in FY 2025-26, up from ₹9,678 crore in FY 2023-24. Karnataka accounts for the largest share of units (34) and exports (₹8,329 crore), followed by Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh. The EHTP scheme is a 100% export-oriented scheme with no dedicated fund allocation, administered by STPI through single-window statutory clearances.
enrichment.context:
The EHTP Scheme, introduced in 1985 alongside the Software Technology Parks (STP) Scheme, aims to promote electronics hardware exports by offering duty-free imports of capital goods and inputs, permission for limited domestic sales, and simplified customs procedures under the Foreign Trade Policy. Unlike production-linked incentive (PLI) schemes that involve direct fiscal outlay, EHTP is a facilitation-based export promotion mechanism with no budgetary allocation, relying instead on tax/duty concessions and procedural ease via the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), which acts as the single-window nodal agency for statutory approvals.

This data point fits into India's broader push to position itself as an electronics manufacturing and export hub, alongside larger initiatives like the PLI scheme for electronics, Semiconductor Mission, and Make in India. While EHTP's export figures (around ₹11,000 crore) are modest compared to India's overall electronics exports (which run into lakhs of crores driven by mobile phone manufacturing under PLI), the scheme remains a legacy mechanism supporting smaller and mid-sized export-oriented hardware units, with continuing concentration in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh reflecting existing electronics manufacturing clusters.

prelims_questions.question: The Electronics Hardware Technology Park (EHTP) Scheme, mentioned in news, is administered on a single-window clearance basis by which agency?
options: Electronics and Computer Software Export Promotion Council (ESC)
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that STPI (Software Technology Parks of India) provides statutory services on a single-window clearance system under the EHTP Scheme.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following statements about the EHTP Scheme is correct?
options: It provides direct budgetary fiscal incentives for setting up electronics export units
It is a 100% export-oriented scheme with no fund allocation from the government
It is a component of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for electronics
It exclusively covers software exports, not hardware
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the EHTP Scheme is a 100% export-oriented scheme with no fund allocation, relying instead on duty exemptions and procedural facilitation under the Foreign Trade Policy.

study_notes.reason: The release is essentially a statistical Lok Sabha reply on EHTP units and exports; the only real UPSC value lies in facts about the scheme's design, nodal agency and figures, with little independent analytical depth beyond generic export-promotion commentary.

prelims.point: EHTP (Electronics Hardware Technology Park) Scheme is a 100% export-oriented scheme introduced in 1985 alongside the STP Scheme, with no dedicated budgetary fund allocation.
prelims.why_important: Distinguishes EHTP from fiscal-outlay schemes like PLI, a classic 'distinguish between similar schemes' UPSC angle.

prelims.point: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is the single-window nodal/statutory clearance agency administering the EHTP Scheme.
prelims.why_important: STPI's role as implementing/nodal agency is a directly testable institutional fact.

prelims.point: EHTP incentives are governed under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, including duty-free import of capital goods/inputs and permitted Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) sales.
prelims.why_important: Links EHTP to the broader Foreign Trade Policy framework, a recurring prelims theme.

prelims.point: Number of EHTP units rose from 70 (FY23-24) to 79 (FY25-26); exports rose from ₹9,678 crore to an estimated ₹11,102 crore over the same period.
prelims.why_important: Quantitative data that could be tested as a factual statement on scheme growth.

prelims.point: Karnataka has the largest number of EHTP units (34) and highest exports (₹8,329 crore) among states/UTs, followed by Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.
prelims.why_important: State-wise ranking is a common prelims-style data question format.

mains.point: EHTP relies on facilitation (duty concessions, single-window clearance) rather than direct fiscal incentives, unlike PLI-type schemes, raising the question of which model better drives export competitiveness for smaller/mid-sized electronics units.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for comparing facilitation-based versus subsidy-based industrial policy instruments in a question on manufacturing/export strategy.

mains.point: Continued geographic concentration of EHTP units in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh reflects uneven regional spread of electronics manufacturing clusters despite decades-old scheme.
mains.analytical_use: Can support an answer on regional imbalances in industrial/export infrastructure and need for cluster diversification.
